authoredPrompt: This figure is a schematic of a single array drawn as a long horizontal strip of equal cells, shaded to mark off four regions. Four italic labels sit above the strip: p over the leftmost cell, i over the fourth cell, j further to the right, and r over the rightmost cell. Three heavy black bars stand between cells as the region boundaries. The four cells from p through i are pale gray; the six cells between the first and second bar are a darker gray; the five cells after the second bar and before the last are white and empty; and the single cell at the right end, under r, is white and holds the italic letter x. Three curly braces beneath the strip label the pale gray stretch as at most x, written with the symbol for less than or equal to followed by x, the dark gray stretch as greater than x, and the white stretch as unrestricted. The shading separates the portion of the array already classified against the pivot from the portion not yet examined. The strip states the invariant holding at the top of each iteration while a subarray is rearranged in place around the pivot value stored at position r.
authoredInteractions:
- Code editor for PARTITION(A, p, r): learner implements the loop using pivot x, indices i and j, compare(A[j], x), and swap primitives; each executed line advances the strip boundaries and updates the <= x, > x, and unrestricted regions.
- Step-through invariant view: before and after every loop iteration, the diagram highlights which cells satisfy the invariant A[p..i] <= x, A[i+1..j-1] > x, and A[j..r-1] unrestricted.
- Test-case toggle: switch the current A[j] between <= x and > x cases to see why one branch swaps and advances i while the other only advances j.

discrepancies: The default view is dominated by a large code-editor/workbench UI that is not present in the source, so the static schematic is no longer the primary visual element at a glance.
The schematic itself is much smaller and lower on the page than the source figure, reducing the prominence of the cells, braces, and labels.
The r label is centered over the final pivot cell rather than being aligned with the thick separator immediately before the x cell as in the source.
The brace labels, especially 'unrestricted', are noticeably smaller and less visually dominant than in the source.
evaluation.notes: The core partition-invariant strip, shading, bars, braces, and labels are structurally very close to the source, but the default presentation is visually overwhelmed by the added workbench and the schematic is undersized.
action_items: Make the source schematic fill the available figure area in the default state, matching the source composition more closely.
Collapse or move the code-editor workbench behind an optional tab/control so the default view reads as a drop-in replacement for the static textbook figure.
Move the r label to align with the thick separator before the final x cell rather than centering it over the pivot cell.
Increase the size and prominence of the underbrace labels, particularly 'unrestricted'.
